title: [PIPELINE VALIDATION] H1: developmental learner vs static persona, memory-only and plain-RL baselines on held-out tasks
hypothesis: Agents whose policy develops from experience (developmental learner) reach higher accuracy on held-out symbols (never seen in practice) than equally-resourced static-persona, memory-only, or plain-RL agents given an identical item and feedback stream.
falsification_criterion: H1 is NOT supported if the developmental learner's mean held-out accuracy fails to exceed the strongest baseline by >=10% (relative) with a paired 95% bootstrap CI excluding zero across 10 independent seeds; it is refuted (failed) if the CI upper bound lies below the 10% threshold.

analysis.primary_metric_definition: Per agent: mean over the three training families (sort, compare, signal) of greedy accuracy on the fixed 60-item held-out set (holdout symbols only, learning disabled, ties credited fractionally) after 300 practice episodes per family; averaged over 20 agents per seed; one value per seed.
analysis.comparison: developmental - strongest baseline, paired by seed

validity_notes: Synthetic task world; held-out = unseen symbols under the same hidden rules, not unseen humans.
Baseline hyperparameters (plain_rl lr=0.05) were tuned on task seeds 1001-1003, never on evaluation seeds 0-9.
The developmental learner's hyperparameters are owned by the research/development lane; if they were tuned on evaluation seeds this result is optimistic.
Age gate (perceptual feature access) is a scripted assumption applied identically to all arms; the no_age_gate sensitivity variant removes it.
